verifiedFindings: The existing Forgive or Forget branch snapshot took 1292.63094 ms for one pure Engine V3 ranking of two legal choice actions. Other six snapshots ranged 14.81643 to 72.08109 ms in this pass.

Sampled stacks include parent bestBranch/chooseCards -> lifecycle assessCardLifecycle -> cardUseValue/assessPublicCardUse -> material assessAlgorithmProjection -> nested bestBranch/applyTargets. Child material probes disable publicCardLifecycle, so the observed nesting is bounded and is not infinite lifecycle recursion.
The material-use cache is allocated inside lifecycleContext per operation and keyed by card.id; repeated equivalent sibling branches do not share that cache.

Forgive or Forget public definition has nested optional max-two discard choices followed by combineBindings/bound purge. The existing snapshot has four actor discard and ten opponent discard cards. The normal 48-set cap allows at most 11*48=528 nested choice-set pairs before shared effect budget and other rules; this is a static capacity, not an instrumented execution count.

Development rows 48,74,78 retain per-game/seat max and histogram but no latency-to-action/observation link. Harness times the guard-wrapped policy call; observation/step and shadow display mutation ranking occur outside that timer.
notEstablished: The exact action, card, public observation or CPU cause of development game 74 max 5079.91788 ms, game 48 max 1178.79147 ms or game 78 max 938.90124 ms is not identifiable from these aggregate records.
The Forgive fixture is from earlier diagnostic game 16 revision 80; it is not a recorded snapshot of development game 74. Public deck membership overlap is only a lead, not causal attribution.
No isolated latency baseline, speedup, strategy quality effect, or significance conclusion is established by this one profiling pass.

nextCandidateSuggestions.description: Share material quality results within one rank call only for exactly equivalent public projected state, physical card/owner, action and targets, features, phase/window, restrictions, counters and bindings. A card-name-only cache or cache across Observations is unsafe. Check identical rankings and no input mutation before performance claims.

Reuse pure board/zone indices and unchanged projected views with an explicit projection version; invalidate on moves, captured/power changes, bindings and restrictions. Current repeated group projection and formula scans appear in samples.

Consider deterministic combined parent/material evaluation budgets with documented approximate fallback. This changes search coverage and requires a new candidate, targeted regressions and a fresh matched comparison; do not patch the current frozen candidate.

Before a new run, record top-K slow policy calls with public Observation hash, action/stage and exact monotonic timestamps. Do not expose hidden state or RNG. Aggregate-only histograms cannot retrospectively attribute an individual slow call.
